# A Short History of Marketing Thought {#sec-history}

<!--

Marketing is a young discipline with an unusually self-conscious history: the field
periodically stops to ask what it is, what counts as knowledge in it, and whom that
knowledge serves. This chapter situates the rest of the book historically—how
marketing thought moved through distinct eras, how its competing "schools" framed
the object of study, and how the discipline's intellectual center of gravity has
shifted between the managerial, the behavioral, and the quantitative. We close with
the sociology of the field today: how doctoral training, the top-4 journals, and the
academic job market shape what gets studied and who studies it.
